# BOOK V. THE PAMPHYLIAN OBELISK

...since we have already explained these symbols often, and they are clear from the following Reading, we did not wish to dwell on them. <margin>Recapitulation of what has been said</margin> But so that these words may be better understood, note that the 1st figure represents **Momphta**, or the Deity who in action traverses all things; the **Asp** which he carries on his head indicates that he animates all things with life, being powerful in his dominion over all; and 4 the **moist substance** 3 is solidified by the staff of **Osiris**. This Momphta, when he is seen prostrate, as in the 2nd Scheme of the 1st Side at number 14, indicates what the priests ought to do in attracting him; he is also sometimes seen hanging, as if in the air, as in the 3rd Scheme of the 1st Side, figure 17; and by this figure he denotes absolute dominion over the watery substance. 

But when he is seen under the form of a **Lion's head**, or the figure of a **crouching lion**, he indicates the protection of the **Nilotic increase** <note>The annual flooding of the Nile, essential for Egyptian agriculture</note>; all of which I wished to declare in this place, lest you be confused by the ambiguity of the name and the figure of Momphta. He is called **Momphta** or **Mophta**, from *mou* and *phe*, or from *mou* and *phet*, of which the former in Egyptian signifies **waters**, and the latter **God**; as if you were to say the **God of the waters**, or the Deity of the moist substance, and he corresponds to **Neptune**, as if you were to say *Mephtuno*. 

Therefore, in these sacrifices, the **gourd** in the form of a club, the **Nilotic urn** hanging from either the neck or the hands, and the **feather** on the head, expressed his duties in the **Worldly Economy** <note>The divine management and maintenance of the physical universe</note>. For they believed that once the Deity was solicited in this way through a mediator, the Supreme **World Spirit** mixed with the lower things became *multiform* <note>original: "πολύμορφον" (polymorphon)</note>; or what is the same, the triform Deity, having fallen from the three superior neighboring Worlds into the three **material worlds**—that is, the Sphere of generation—moderated all things there as if in the **realm of Morpheus** <note>The realm of forms, dreams, and changing appearances</note>. There **Anubis**, the faithful and vigilant minister of the said Deity, destroys the malignant **Typhonian force**, indicated by the iron of the lance. 

For as **Plutarch** rightly shows, the Egyptians used to exhibit this Deity in **Hermopolis** (that is, the City of Mercury) through a man transfixing a **Hippopotamus** (that is, **Typhon**) with a lance; see the reasons for this explained at length on page 465. Furthermore, they believed this Deity goes about in the form of a **dog**, teaching men **astrology**, and announcing various future events to men through divinations and dreams; therefore, with peculiar study and care, he was accustomed to be worshiped in the solemnity of the **Comasiae** <note>original: "Comasiarum," referring to religious processions where statues of gods were carried</note> as something divine and the presiding power of wise speech. 

But because they knew that the said concatenated Deities do not easily comply with those calling upon them, they arranged the following **sacred table**, in which a **Hawk** is seen with a **young goat** in whose beak is a herb—which I interpret as **hawkweed** <note>original: "hieracium," a plant associated in lore with hawks sharpening their sight</note>—along with a **triangle**, a **Spheroid**, and the figure of a **crouching Lion**. By these they indicated that the **Supreme Osiris** is the guardian of vegetable nature; just as he sows the genital principles into the heavens, so these, derived and actuated from there into the kingdom of **Mophta**, grant the desired fertility. Through these mediating Deities, the rest of the crowd of concatenated Deities, under the protection of the **triform Deity**, easily present themselves, as is clear from the following Reading.

## Ideal Contextual Reading.

The one performing the sacrifice is also equipped with sacred attire: the staff, the **club of Mophta**, the **feather of Osiris**, and an **amulet of the sacred liquid**.

For by these means, the **world spirit** <note>Latin: *spiritus mundanus*, often referring to the *Anima Mundi* or life force connecting the heavens and earth</note> is channeled into the **Elemental World**, becoming **multiform** <note>original: πολυμορφος (polymorphos)</note>, or ready to be transformed into every shape of lower things.

The **Triform Deity**, descending from the three supernal Worlds into the Elemental worlds—or the sphere of generation—appointed **Anubis** as the sacred guardian of celestial things. He is the carrier and bringer of **astrological impressions** <note>the influence of the stars and planets upon the physical world</note>, to be worshipped with all honor; and this truly is a sacred and wisely instituted amulet.

### *A Sacred Table showing the amulet.*

**Osiris** is the author of fecundity and of all vegetation; the **Sacred Mophta** draws the power of this generation from heaven into his own Kingdom.

BOOK V. THE PAMPHYLIAN OBELISK

## SCHEME VI.
### Of the fourth Northern Side.

<margin>What the seated statue signifies.</margin>
<margin>What the triple tiaras of three diverse forms represent.</margin>
<margin>The sacred table.</margin>
In this Diagram, following the Sacred Table, there is a **mystagogic figure** <note>a "mystagogue" is one who interprets or leads others into sacred mysteries</note> in the posture $^1$ of a **seated man**. This is followed by a $^2$ **serpent-bearing globe** with a $^4$ **quadrangle**, then a $^5$ **vessel** <note>original: *crater*, referring to a mixing bowl used in rituals</note> with three $^6$ $^7$ $^8$ **tiaras** <note>ceremonial headdresses or crowns</note> of different shapes. To once again attract the **World Spirit** <note>Latin: *spiritus mundanus*, the vital force connecting the divine and material worlds</note>, these require a seated statue with feet set apart, resting upon the sacred vessel. This is meant to indicate the attraction of the **Deity** <note>original: *Numinis*</note> into the sacred vessel—a Deity, I say, eminent in its triple power. The first tiara shows a **polymorphic power** <note>original: *polymorpham*, meaning "many-shaped" or versatile</note> over all things; the second, a **Solar power** over vegetation, indicated by a basket-like crown; the third, a **Lunar power**, indicated by a gourd-shaped crown. 

Next follows another **prophylactic amulet** <note>an object used for protection against evil or disease</note> which they believed possessed great virtue for deriving this triple power into the lower things. It is marked by the following symbols: $^9$ a **scalene triangle** with an $^{10}$ **extended arm**, and $^{11}$ $^{13}$ **two double-knotted scepters** joined by a $^{12}$ **spheroid**. These are followed by $^{14}$ **two feathers** with the $^{15}$ **scepter of Mophta** <note>an Egyptian spirit Kircher associates with the power of water and humidity</note>, an $^{16}$ **extended arm** with a $^{17}$ **Nilotic urn** <note>a vessel used to hold water from the Nile</note>, a $^{19}$ **double-knotted scepter**, and $^{18}$ **feathers**. After these comes a $^{20}$ **Ram** before a $^{21}$ **seated mystagogic statue**, both of which stand upon a $^{22}$ **double-knotted scepter**. The symbols conclude with a **segment** and a **double-knotted scepter**. 

By these symbols, through a certain silent invocation, they request that the beneficial force of generation be channeled: first through the power of the heavens into the Aerial World, then through the beneficial kingdom of **Mophta**, then into the nature of moisture, and finally into the fertile **Kingdom of Ammon** <note>Ammon, or Amun, often symbolized by the ram, representing fertility and hidden power</note>, which they indicate by the **Ram of Ammon**. Since the reasoning for each of these has been made clear in the preceding pages, we have decided not to repeat them here. 

There are also **two mystagogic statues**: the first $^{23}$ is of **Horus** in the form of a seated boy equipped with a **Cucucomorphous scepter** <note>Kircher's term for the *Was*-scepter, which he believed resembled a hoopoe bird (cucuma)</note>; the second $^{24}$ is of **Isis**, distinguished by a sacred veil and a spiked headdress with an inserted globe, holding a **lotus flower** in her hand. These mystical statues are placed upon a $^{25}$ **bier** <note>original: *feretrum*, a litter used to carry idols in a procession</note> to represent the rites, ceremonies, and processions with which the said Deities ought to be honored, along with $^{26}$ **charms** <note>original: *periaptis*, amulets worn on the body</note> to be worn for warding off evils and for obtaining what they seek in their sacred rites.

You see, therefore, in this entire Diagram, that nothing else is indicated but the method by which the **World Spirit** must be attracted into the sacred vessel—that is, the **moist substance of the universe**—through the appropriate statue and through the sacred table equipped with mystical apparatus. It shows how a triple benefit emanates from the triple power granted to the World Spirit by the Supreme Deity. Furthermore, it details which ceremonies must be conducted through the **Processions of the Comasia** <note>referring to ancient Egyptian festival processions</note> and solemnities to procure the attraction of the Deity.

### INTERPRETATION.

### Context of the Ideal Reading.

From here, through the $^1$ **image** <note>Latin: *simulacrum*, a representation or statue</note> the $^3$ **spirit** $^2$ of the **World** <note>Latin: *Spiritus Mundi*, the vital breath or soul of the universe in Hermetic philosophy</note> is drawn into the $^5$ **lower** $^4$ **vessel** <note>original: *crater*, a mixing bowl or receptacle for divine influence</note>: the $^7$ **triple** $^7$ **power** of the **Supreme Deity** $^6$ passes into the **moist, many-shaped** <note>original: *polymorphum*, referring to the ever-changing nature of the material world</note> realm; by which he grants power, and the following amulet <note>original: *periaptum*, a protective charm or hanging symbol</note> of the sacred table. $^9$ The **beneficent** $^{11}$ **Presider** $^{10}$ over **Generation**, $^{13}$ **possessing fourfold power** $^{12}$ in the **celestial dominion**, commits the $^{17}$ **beneficent** $^{19}$ **airy** $^{18}$ **moisture** through $^{15}$ **Mophta** <note>A name used by Kircher for a specific Egyptian genius or elemental power associated with the air and humidity</note> $^{16}$ to $^{20}$ **Ammon** <note>The deity Amun, here presented as the ruler of the lower physical realms</note> who is $^{22}$ **most powerful** in the **lower regions**, who is drawn through the $^{21}$ **image** and appropriate ceremonies to exert his power.

From this, if the priests adapt the $^{23}$ $^{24}$ **sacred statues** with a $^{25}$ **mystical apparatus** analogous for attracting the Gods, the spirit of the said Deities $^{26}$ will be drawn through an influx from the $^{27}$ **supernal** into the $^{28}$ **lower world**, and life will be spent immune from all evils and $^{29}$ **adversities**, and perpetual happiness will be acquired, which is the end of the entire sacred hieroglyphic doctrine.

### BOOK IV. THE PAMPHYLIAN OBELISK

And these are the things which—so far as the constraints of time permitted—we thought should be said concerning the mysteries of the Pamphylian Obelisk <note>The Pamphylian Obelisk is the granite monument now located in the Piazza Navona in Rome; Kircher believed its hieroglyphs contained a lost system of ancient wisdom.</note>. Many other matters concerning the **analogical, tropological, and political senses** <note>These represent different layers of interpretation: analogical (spiritual/heavenly), tropological (moral/behavioral), and political (social/civil order).</note> have been omitted; any person skilled in **symbolic doctrine** will be able to apply these to the sequences of the other worlds with no effort. In the meantime, let it suffice to have given the curious reader in this place some specimen of the interpretation of those things primarily intended by the Egyptians.

---

->C O N C L V S I O N.<-

MOREOVER, since this little ship of ours—as if having crossed a sea far too spacious and vast, and having overcome great difficulties like rolling waves by the gracious help of GOD—has now arrived at its destination, it remains for us to offer our thanks to the supreme Author of all good things and most generous Giver. If we cannot give the thanks we owe, let us at least give what we can, and confess before all living things Him who has shown His mercy toward us. *For it is good to hide the secret of a king; but to reveal and confess the works of GOD is honorable.* <note>A quotation from the Book of Tobit 12:7.</note> Therefore, to the supreme King of the Ages, immortal and invisible, the Holy Trinity—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one GOD—from whom, in whom, and through whom all things exist, and without whom we can do nothing good, nor even think it: all honor and glory.

Next, to You, Savior of the human race, <term>Θεανθρώπῳ</term> <note>original Greek: *Theanthrōpō*, meaning the "God-Man."</note> Jesus Christ, who has deigned to lead these labors of whatever sort to their desired end; You who bestowed a copious gift of grace upon your little servant so that I might complete a work far beyond my own strength. Just as You are Eternal Truth, uncreated Wisdom, and the Word of the Eternal Father, so too You have illuminated my dark soul with Your light, visited it with grace, lifted up my mind, stirred my spirit, and provided aid.

To You also, Eternal Love, Supreme Spirit, who, brooding over the dark moisture of my soul, stirred me with the love of heavenly things, breathed life into the offspring of my mind, and inspired me—even when I was not yet willing—so that I might will, and helped the efforts of my good will so that I might act; You who work both the willing and the perfecting in Your own people.

Finally, I give thanks to the Virgin Mother of God, the dispenser of divine gifts, truly <term>ἀθανασίῳ</term> <note>original Greek: *athanasiō*, meaning "immortal" or "undying."</note>, through whose kindness, merits, and intercession I profess and rejoice to have obtained such great grace. Lastly, I confess my debt to the Holy Guardian Angel divinely appointed to me, who was always present with hidden promptings and provided the opportunity so that I might be able to achieve what I desired.

I am not unaware that many things in this work will please, and many will displease. Let the latter be attributed to me, but the former <term>πάντα εἰς</term> <note>original Greek: *panta eis*, meaning "all things [directed] to..."</note> the Spirit and the Father of Lights, GOD, without whose protection all human wisdom rightly becomes foolishness, and all efforts of human genius fail, becoming void and useless—vanishing like the thin dross that is winnowed on the threshing floor.

Finally, if anything contrary to orthodox doctrine has escaped me against my mind and intention, I wish it retracted; and thus, let all my works be subject to the judgment of the Holy Roman Church. Farewell.

# NOTE TO THE READER

->Concerning the Errors committed in this Work.<-

Kind reader, I had intended to bring this present work to light as corrected as humanly possible—since it is a new work, filled with exotic terms and a variety of languages—by employing three Correctors to spend their effort on correcting the typeset. However, despite applying all possible diligence, it was not possible to avoid this usual Scylla <note>A reference to the unavoidable sea monster of Greek myth; a common metaphor for a persistent danger or difficult obstacle</note>; for during the final revision of the already printed work, we discovered not a few errors, not without great mental anguish. Regardless, lest these errors be attributed to my own sluggishness, I have decided to join them here, collected into one place, so that the corrected book might be restored to its integrity.

Therefore, correct the faults as follows: the first number denotes the Page, the second the line.
